Local News
SummaryStorm Boelo will bring more wet and windy weather to large parts of the UK on Saturday - a day after Storm Austen hit the country
Yellow warnings begin in Northern Ireland from 10:00 BST, while amber warnings for northern England, Scotland, and parts of Northern Ireland begin at 21:00 BST
Gusts are forecast to reach 60-70mph widely and could reach 80mph in exposed locations - see the latest forecast in our video rail
On Friday, Austen hit southern England, the Channel Islands, and parts of Wales
Tens of thousands of properties lost power in south-west England - hundreds are still waiting to be reconnected on Saturday

Flooding expected in Scarborough and part of Staffordshirepublished at 09:13 BST09:13 BST Image source, mrbyorkshire/BBC Weather WatchersImage caption, The Environment Agency warns further flooding is "expected" in Scarborough later today. For now, there's little cloud in the skyThree flood warnings and 14 flood alerts are in place across England - a flood warning indicates flooding is "expected", while an alert means it is "possible".Flooding expected At Foreshore Road in Scarborough, where high tides already caused flooding on Friday evening - leaving some vehicles stranded and forcing roads to close
High tides were also expected to cause flooding at Sandside in Scarborough and people are encouraged to avoid coastal roads, footpaths and carparks at both locations
From yesterday evening, rising river levels were expected to cause flooding at Saredon Brook in Standeford, an area in Staffordshire

Strong winds and heavy rain expected to cause rail disruption in Scotlandpublished at 08:33 BST08:33 BST Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Storm Boelo is expected to disrupt travel around Scotland today and on SundayWe can now bring you some more details on the cancelled train services ScotRail has already announced. They are: Glasgow Central – Ayr line will close between Kilwinning and Ayr from 21:00 on Saturday, after which time a half-hourly shuttle service will operate between Glasgow Central and Kilwinning
Glasgow Queen Street – Oban / Mallaig line will close between Fort William and Mallaig and between Crianlarich and Oban from around 22:00

When do we see the most named storms?published at 08:14 BST08:14 BSTChris FawkesBBC Weather presenter Image source, BBC WeatherImage caption, The winter months of December, January and February typically produce the highest number of UK stormsAlthough named storms can affect the UK at any time of the year, analysis shows they are much less common in spring and early summer.The only month with no named storms in the eleven years that we've been naming storms in the UK is May.The chances of seeing a storm increases from late summer and throughout autumn with the peak of the season arriving in our winter months.This increase in storminess is why the storm-naming season begins in September each year.In about half of the years since 2015, the first storm arrived after 1 November. South-west battled wet and windy weather as Storm Austen hitpublished at 07:57 BST07:57 BST The UK is bracing for its second storm in two days, with the north hunkering down for Storm Boelo as the south-west recovers from Storm Austen. Here are some pictures from yesterday when Austen hit southern England, parts of Wales, and the Channel Islands, with gusts of up to 84mph recorded in Jersey.Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Waves break at Portland Bill in DorsetImage source, PA MediaImage caption, Pieces of Brighton's iconic West Pier fell off into the sea during the wet and windy weatherImage caption, Trees fell and fences were damaged by high winds in the Channel Islands Shareclose panelShare pageCopy linkAbout sharing
How to prepare for power cutspublished at 07:43 BST07:43 BST Image source, Getty ImagesAs well as travel disruptions being expected from Storm Boelo, some properties in areas under warning could be left without power.Power cuts can plunge communities into darkness and stop usual services from working, but here are some helpful tips on how to navigate an outage: Candles and torches can replace lights during power cuts, although it's important to remember naked flames can pose a fire risk
Keep cash on hand as shops may not accept phone and card payments when the power is out
Tinned food and gas stoves will help keep you fed as microwaves, air fryers and some hobs and ovens demand electricity
Powerbanks can help keep your phone charged, allowing you to see the latest updates
You can report a power cut online,, external or by calling 105, which is a free service in England, Scotland and Wales.
Hundreds of properties still without power in south-west Englandpublished at 07:30 BST07:30 BST Hundreds of homes and businesses are still without power after Storm Austen battered parts of the country yesterday.National Grid's map shows a concentration of power cuts in south-west England, the area worst affected by the storm. In Cornwall, one incident near Truro has left 478 properties without power, while another near Penryn is affecting 127 properties. One incident in Dorset is impacting 141 properties, with another 85 properties in Exmoor still without power. Both of these are not estimated to be resolved until 22:00 tonight, according to National Grid's website.These are just a few examples from the swarm of red and blue incident dots seen on the map.Image source, National Grid Shareclose panelShare pageCopy linkAbout sharing
Storm Boelo expected to cause widespread travel disruption across Scotland and north of Englandpublished at 07:15 BST07:15 BST Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, ScotRail says speed restrictions will be in place on some routes, with some services not running and cancellations possible as Storm Boelo hitsNational Rail is warning that Storm Boelo may impact journeys and encouraging people to check before they travel.It says: TransPennine Express is advising against anything but essential travel today and on Sunday - while there are no planned changes to the timetable today, speed restrictions will be in place across Scotland. Widespread disruption is expected on Sunday
Avanti West Coast is advising people to avoid travelling north of Preston on Sunday
LNER is advising against travel between Edinburgh and Aberdeen on Sunday
Northern will see a reduction in the number of trains operating on several routes today
Speed restrictions will be in place on certain ScotRail routes today, some services will not run and there will be cancellations of revisions across the entire network from 21:00 tonight - we've got more on Scottish travel disruption here
CrossCountry says services travelling to or from areas north of Newcastle will face a speed restriction today and tomorrow
Although there is no Met Office weather warning over Wales today, Transport for Wales is warning of weather-related disruption to its network - Wales was hit by Storm Austen yesterday
Services in other parts of the country including Great Western are also warning there could be ongoing disruption today because of Storm Austen.
Is it unusual to see two storms so close together?published at 07:02 BST07:02 BSTChris FawkesBBC Weather presenter It's not unusual to get storms so close together, in fact they quite often arrive in clusters.A strong jet stream is needed to rapidly develop powerful wind storms. The process of creating such storms involves shifting warmer air northwards and cooler air southwards across vast areas of the Atlantic.These temperature contrasts can provide a fertile environment for new low pressure systems to develop and if these subsequently get steered beneath a developmental area of a powerful jet stream, they can rapidly develop to create a new named storm with damaging winds. How much disruption was caused by Storm Austenpublished at 06:50 BST06:50 BST Image source, ReutersStorm Austen caused major disruption across parts of England and Wales on Friday - here's a recap: Thousands of homes were left without power, and gusts of up to 84mph (135km/h) were recorded in Jersey
In Brighton, dramatic footage captured the collapse of part of the iconic West Pier as it fell into the sea
All schools on Jersey and Guernsey closed for the day and some in Cornwall were closed or started later than normal
Transport was also disrupted, with some ferry services between the UK and France cancelled and trains cancelled and delayed
Jersey Airport said flights wouldn't be running until at least 17:00 on Friday, while departure boards at Exeter airport also showed multiple cancellations
The damage caused to a car hit by a tree in Horsham, West Sussex, on Friday
Amber and yellow wind warnings in place for Scotland, northern England and Northern Irelandpublished at 06:42 BST06:42 BST Image source, Met OfficeYellowA yellow wind warning is in place for Scotland and northern England from midday today until 21:00 tomorrow, while another warning covers Northern Ireland from 10:00 today to 12:00 tomorrow.AmberThe Met Office has issued an amber wind warning for Scotland, north-eastern parts of Northern Ireland, and parts of northern England, running from 21:00 tonight to 21:00 tomorrow.The national forecaster warns that flying debris is likely and could lead to injuries or danger to life. It also warns of transport disruption, power cuts and dangerous coastal conditions. Very strong westerly winds are expected with fairly widespread gusts of 60 to 70 mph and gusts to 80 mph in exposed coastal areas. Shareclose panelShare pageCopy linkAbout sharing
Storm Boelo to bring 80mph winds as second storm hits UKpublished at 06:35 BST06:35 BST Image source, ReutersImage caption, Waves crash over the lighthouse at Newhaven Harbour in East SussexA second storm is set to hit the UK today, bringing strong winds and heavy rain to much of the country.Storm Boelo, the second named storm of the season, could cause travel disruption and power cuts on Saturday, with wind gusts of 60-70mph forecast, while exposed coastal areas could see speeds of up to 80mph.It comes just hours after Storm Austen swept across the country, leaving more than 60,000 homes without power in England and Wales, and causing school closures in Cornwall, Jersey and Guernsey.The Met Office has issued amber and yellow warnings for wind on Saturday and Sunday to cover parts of Scotland, Northern Ireland and northern England.The strongest winds are expected in Scotland from Saturday evening, extending eastwards through Sunday, according to the weather agency.Train operators across the country have warned that services are likely to be disrupted over the weekend.Stick with us for the latest weather warnings and travel updates throughout the day.
